title: Export Inspector service: on-demand debug streams and per-tenant export replay
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Provide an internal 'Export Inspector' microservice and API that lets engineers and support perform safe, auditable on-demand replays and live debug streams of customer usage export pipelines. The service must be read-only, tenant-aware, honor RBAC, and produce ephemeral signed artifacts (preview CSVs, replay manifests, or streaming debug sessions) without performing any write-side mutations to customer data or export delivery endpoints.
background: Customer support and infra teams currently spend significant time reproducing export delivery issues: missing rows, encoding errors, and intermittent S3 403/timeout failures. Existing tools are limited to raw S3 manifests and manual Kafka replay. We need a first-class debugging surface that ties export manifests -> CDC/replay -> packaged previews and live debug streams so engineers can triage faster and customers (for elevated support tiers) can get verifiable previews of what was delivered.
proposed_solution: 1) New service 'export-inspector' deployed in the Console backend namespace. 2) API endpoints: /inspect/manifest (generate preview CSV from manifest), /replay/session (start a read-only CDC replay with filters), /signed-download (ephemeral signed URL for preview files). 3) Implementation reuses existing export manifests store and CDC topic consumer but runs in isolated read-only mode with strict rate limits. 4) Auth: enforce SSO + role check and create audit log entry for every operation. 5) Feature-flag rollout via runtime 'export_inspector_beta' keyed per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria:
- Engineers can generate a 10k-row CSV preview from any completed export manifest within 90s (for typical manifests).
- Support can start a replay session scoped to a tenant + time range and stream rows to the console UI without affecting production exporters.
- Every inspector action is logged to audit logs and surfaces in the Console 'Support Activity' dashboard.
- Signed preview URLs expire within 15 minutes by default and are single-use.
- No write path to customer export destinations is exercised by inspector; all operations are read-only (security review sign-off required).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Internal-only rollout for SRE & Support (feature flag on). Phase 2: Beta with 3 pilot tenants (support + PM outreach). Phase 3: GA for all tenants on paid plans with opt-in. Monitoring and kill-switch in place. Coordinate with Legal for data access policy for previews.
risks:
- Potential cost: generating previews for large manifests increases S3 egress and compute. Mitigation: preview sampling, capped row limits and a per-tenant daily quota.
- Data exposure: ephemeral previews are sensitive; must enforce RBAC and short TTLs.
- Replaying against CDC may interfere with consumer offsets if misconfigured; implement read-only consumer group with no offset commits and run in separate cluster namespace.
- Performance regression risk for the export-manifest store; ensure inspector reads use read-replicas or a cached snapshot.
comments: 2025-02-19 - Aisha Kapoor: Initial RFC posted to Confluence and shared with Support. Requesting SRE input on read-replica access patterns.

2025-02-22 - Marcus Chen (SRE): Agreed on read-only consumer group. Suggested adding a per-tenant preview budget and metric to track preview egress. Also flagged need for a kill-switch if preview generation spikes costs.

2025-02-26 - Luis Ortega: Started service scaffold and added integration test harness for manifest->preview conversion. Found edge cases with multi-encoding CSV rows (UTF-8 vs Latin-1) — adding normalization step.
2025-03-01 - Priya Raman (Security): Security review kickoff; requesting proof that signed URLs are single-use and TTL enforced. Also requested threat model for preview leak scenarios.

2025-03-03 - Luis Ortega: Implemented TTL + nonce for signed downloads. Performance test results: 1k-row previews average 3.2s, 50k-row extrapolated to ~38s under sample run; will add sampling pipeline to avoid full materialization for very large manifests.
